verdicts.argument: In round 1 I held the wording change and attacked the sizing. The obviousness skeptic's sources check out. The 2026-06 Lilly press release p.1 gives the Bridge end date ('December 31, 2027'; verify_quote true). The Q4 2025 transcript p.1 (grade C) has the CFO saying 'these price concessions will be more than offset by increased volume' (verify_quote true). So both legs were said in public. On my lens, nothing in a filed period carries a deal-specific number either: the Bridge started 7/1/2026, and the -10% (FY2025) and -5% (H1 2026) U.S. price lines are mostly pre-deal or cash-pay. That leaves no sizable, unsaid remainder.
verdicts.correction: Kill as a nugget. If the consensus angle is kept, it is a valuation view: I/B/E/S FY2028 EPS rose from $49.53 (2026-03-19) to $53.97 (2026-08-20), and that view relies on Medicare access that is guaranteed only through 12/31/2027. It is not a filing finding.

round2.conceded: The Bridge end date and the volume-offsets-price claim are in a Lilly press release and Q4 2025 prepared remarks. My round-1 'held' rested on the wording drift, which adds no new fact.
round2.held: The $3.0B and $965M figures should not be called deal concessions. That math problem stands whatever the verdict.

The other skeptic adds that FY2025 also inserted 'may result in supply imbalances', which is correct per 10-K FY2025 p.34. It also dropped the 2024 shortage example. Neither change carries a number. verdicts.argument: I concede the main legs. Orforglipron was approved in the U.S. in April 2026 (Q1 2026 call p.1: 'orforgopron was approved by the U.S.'). The 10-Q 2026Q2 inventory note (p.15) no longer carries a pre-launch line. Pre-launch inventory was disclosed in every filing: $548.1M in the FY2024 10-K p.75 and $952.3M in the 10-Q 2025Q3 p.18 (verified). Breen asked about it on the record. So the $1.5B write-off downside ($1.34/share) is stale and the topic is said. My round-1 point that the receivable gap reversed by mid-2026 also stands. One version is both material and not said in anything I checked: inventory keeps outgrowing cost of sales after launch. On the 10-Q 2026Q2 p.5 and p.7 and 10-Q 2025Q2 p.7, Q2 2026 inventory of 16,793 against annualized Q2 COGS of 13,072 gives 469 days, up from 410 days a year earlier (11,013.8 / 9,792). Inventory rose +52.5% and Q2 COGS +33.5%. At the year-ago days, inventory would be about $14.7B, so the excess is about $2.1B of working capital. WIP is $9,997M, 60% of the total (p.15). This is a cash-flow and write-down-risk item worth about 10% of FY2025 net income of $20.6B. It is not an EPS item unless written down. Management talks in doses produced (1.8x), not inventory days.
verdicts.correction: Kill the pre-launch and receivables framing. A narrow survivor: inventory days on COGS rose from 410 to 469 year over year at June 2026, after orforglipron approval, with WIP 60% of inventory. That is about $2.1B above the year-ago days. It is material to cash, and the transcripts I checked do not state it, but it has no EPS effect today.

round2.conceded: Foundayo approval makes the write-off downside stale. Pre-launch stock was disclosed every quarter and asked about. I had held c03 as minor; it is refuted as written.
round2.held: The DIO arithmetic was right. The receivables reversal I found in round 1 also kills the receivables leg.
round2.narrowed: To post-approval inventory days, 410 to 469 (about $2.1B of excess working capital), with WIP at 60%.

verdicts.argument: I concede the true-up is said. The Q2 2026 transcript p.1 (grade C) has 'Excluding these adjustments, U.S. price declined by 9%', and the CFO says the adjustments 'we don't expect will continue into the second part of the year.' Q1 2026 (grade D) has the same. The 2025 roll-forward re-widening (57.7% to 58.8%) is the same fact as the -10% 2025 U.S. price line (10-K p.49), which is headline. I do not accept the other skeptic's surviving narrow claim. 'Liability +45% vs Q2 U.S. revenue +33%' compares the consolidated balance-sheet liability (10-Q p.7), which is 13% ex-U.S. per 10-K p.54, with U.S.-only revenue. Against consolidated Q2 revenue (+47.7%, 10-Q p.5) the liability grew more slowly. The U.S.-only roll-forward is disclosed only annually, so the U.S. comparison cannot be built for June 2026 from filings.
verdicts.correction: No version of the gross-to-net finding is both material and unsaid. The material part ($1.2B of 2025 widening, the $432M Q2 true-up) is said. The unsaid part (the liability outrunning sales) is a denominator error.

round2.conceded: The true-up and the 2025 price-driven GTN widening are in prepared remarks every quarter, so my round-1 held is withdrawn.
round2.held: The obviousness skeptic's surviving narrow claim fails on math: consolidated liability against U.S. revenue.

verdicts.argument: We agree the insulin decline is visible on p.65 and that the reporting change was never mentioned on a call. But the obviousness skeptic's correction repeats the error I flagged: 'Other products $22.9B (35% of revenue) from $3.4B (7.5%).' The FY2025 10-K p.49 itself restates 2024 'Other products' as $23,270M, so the like-for-like change is -1.4%. The 'from $3.4B' is a definition change, not a move in revenue. The visibility loss is real, but the products moved into the bucket (legacy insulins, Cyramza, Erbitux, Tyvyt, Olumiant, Emgality, Zyprexa) totalled about $8.0B in FY2024 (10-K FY2024 p.49), or 18% of revenue, and are mostly flat or declining.
verdicts.correction: If kept, state it as: the FY2025 10-K stopped naming ten products that together were about 18% of FY2024 revenue, with no restatement of totals. Never cite 7.5% to 35%. It is non-obvious but low-value on materiality, since the only quantified decline is -$449M (0.7% of revenue), visible on p.65.

round2.conceded: It is unmentioned on calls, so it passes the obviousness test.
round2.held: Refuted as written. The 7.5% to 35% comparison mixes definitions in both the candidate and the other skeptic's correction.
round2.narrowed: To the plain count of products dropped and their FY2024 revenue share (about 18%).

verdicts.argument: Materiality on my math. The booked-versus-maximum gap is $5,292M - $2,167M = $3,125M (10-Q p.13). The FY2026 I/B/E/S EPS mean is $36.45 (2026-08-20). The full gap after a 19.9% tax shield is $2.80/share; with no shield, since remeasurement is often non-deductible, it is $3.50. That is 7.7% to 9.6% of one year's EPS, or 8.6% of annualized pretax income (H1 2026 pretax $18,097M x 2 = $36.2B, 10-Q p.5). But three things shrink it. (1) It is a ceiling, reached only if every Kelonia and Centessa milestone pays out. Fair value is already probability-weighted, so the expected incremental charge is close to zero, and the tail outcome coincides with the acquired IPR&D succeeding. (2) It is spread over the milestone timeline, which runs years, so the per-year EPS hit is a fraction of the ceiling. (3) Lilly's non-GAAP EPS, which I/B/E/S likely tracks, may exclude remeasurement; that is unverified here. The $814M current portion is a cash outflow already booked as a liability, so it is not a P&L charge. It is 2.2% of annualized pretax income and small next to the $13.3B paid for business development in 2026 (10-Q p.31). The obviousness skeptic's '$814M due within a year' repeats wording I flagged: it is fair value classified as current, not a fixed amount owed.
verdicts.correction: Hold, minor. Present it as a disclosed tail: up to about $3.1B ($2.80 to $3.50/share, 8% to 10% of one year's EPS) of future remeasurement charges if every Kelonia and Centessa milestone hits, spread over several years, with an expected value near zero. The $814M is classified current, not 'due'. It passes the 1% bar only as a ceiling, not as an expected impact.

round2.conceded: Unmentioned on calls (the obviousness lens). It is the best survivor here.
round2.held: Minor severity: as an expected value it is not material; only the ceiling is.
round2.narrowed: Sized as a ceiling with a period, and the $814M is restated as current classification.

verdicts.argument: I concede both points. The Q4 2025 transcript p.1 (grade C) has the CFO saying 'Our effective tax rate was 19.7%' (verify_quote true), so the step-up was said and priced in. The prepaid tax pool peaked at $18.69B on 9/30/2025 (10-Q 2025Q3 p.26, verified), then fell to $12.9B (YE2025), $11.8B (Q1 2026, 10-Q 2026Q1 p.14) and $13.6B (June 2026). My round-1 point that it rose 82% in step with inventory used a cherry-picked endpoint: inventory kept rising while prepaid tax fell $5.8B from its peak. The $0.94 math is correct but describes a disclosed, priced fact.
verdicts.correction: Kill. The only remainder (tariff or onshoring effects on Irish prepaid tax) is speculative and unsized.

round2.conceded: The ETR was stated on the call. The prepaid-tax link to inventory was wrong across the peak.
round2.held: The $0.94/share arithmetic and the H1-over-H1 correction.

verdicts.argument: The two lenses agree: the Ricks quote concerns Cigna's model, and the Breen question was answered. Nothing to add.

round2.conceded: The added Q1 2026 re-ask by Breen confirms the topic was said.

verdicts.argument: I accept the narrowing to the label asymmetry. The other skeptic's new source caps materiality further. In the Q3 2025 transcript p.1 (grade B) Yuffa says 'Medicare Part D is a small proportion of our overall volume' (verified, line in context). Today's Medicare share of Zepbound is therefore small, and Bridge volume only begins in Q3 2026, so the reported base at risk is near zero. The size of the risk is about the 2028 negotiation, not current revenue.
verdicts.correction: A label-asymmetry risk to post-2027 Medicare coverage, unsized. Sensitivity is about $180M per 1% of Zepbound U.S. revenue (10-Q p.29). Management says Part D is a small share of volume today.

round2.conceded: Drop the Bridge end date as a reveal. The Part D share is small per management.
round2.held: Not refuted. The asymmetry is real and unsaid, but it does not meet the materiality bar today.
round2.narrowed: To a future coverage risk with no current revenue at risk.

verdicts.argument: The other skeptic shows that the gap is the announced price structure: the 2025-11-06 press release p.1 says the multi-dose pen is '$299, with additional doses up to $449' (verified). That supports my round-1 point that this is a new lower-list SKU, not a reset of existing prices, and that NADAC cannot be mapped to net revenue.

verdicts.argument: I accept the narrowing. The CV/MASH gap matters only through c09, which is unsized. The Foundayo 9 mg cap with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (label p.6) is real fine print but has no revenue number. Zepbound is still the material product at 21% of H1 2026 revenue (10-Q p.29, p.5).
verdicts.correction: Lead with the Zepbound vs Wegovy CV/MASH gap (c09 form) and the Foundayo CYP3A4 cap. Drop food timing.

round2.conceded: Food timing is Lilly's marketing line.
round2.narrowed: To the CV/MASH gap and the CYP3A4 cap.

overall: After round 2 nothing on LLY is both material and unsaid at EPS scale. c06 survives only as a ceiling ($2.80 to $3.50/share across several years, with an expected value near zero), and c09 only as an unsized 2028 coverage risk. The one new survivor from my lens is narrow and cash-only: post-approval inventory days rose from 410 to 469 year over year at June 2026, about $2.1B of excess working capital. Every gross-to-net version is either said (true-ups, 2025 widening) or a denominator error (liability against U.S. revenue).
